name: Beauty Pill
label: Dischord
lede: Chad Clark's shape-shifting band has outlived a hostile audience, a virus in his heart, an album recorded in front of museum crowds, and a transplant, and it keeps changing shape.

eras.title: What came after Smart Went Crazy
eras.text: Smart Went Crazy had won over DC's post-hardcore crowd with Con Art in 1997. When it came apart, its singer, a studio obsessive named Chad Clark, started something Dischord's bio calls a shape-shifting musical project, with his vision and constant change as its only fixed parts.

years.h: Out of the ashes of [[Smart Went Crazy|d9c78028-a30b-470b-b964-2f85cab51cc2]]
years.p: [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] and Abram Goodrich start Beauty Pill and invite Joanne Gholl to make an EP with them.

years.h: Beauty Pill's The Cigarette Girl from the Future · Dischord No. 128.5
years.p: Beauty Pill's first EP, co-released by Dischord and DeSoto Records. The same year Chad Clark mastered [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]]'s Super/System for Dischord.

eras.title: The wrong room
eras.text: As a quintet with Rachel Burke's voice out front, Beauty Pill made two records that sound, now, like a band too far ahead of its audience. Dischord's crowd wanted the old post-hardcore; Clark would later link the whole era to the feeling of failing.

years.h: [[Rachel Burke|1fd466ef-ace6-4e44-bf53-aa0ef692908e]] joins, and Beauty Pill becomes a quintet
years.p: Rachel Burke joins Chad Clark's Beauty Pill on vocals, with Basla Andolsun on bass, Drew Doucette on guitar and [[Ryan Nelson|758a01ba-b700-4b52-809a-917da0bb30e5]] on drums.

years.h: Beauty Pill's You Are Right to Be Afraid · Dischord No. 138
years.p: Beauty Pill's second EP, and the second of its three Dischord releases in four years.

years.h: Beauty Pill's The Unsustainable Lifestyle · Dischord No. 139
years.p: Beauty Pill's first full-length, and its last record on Dischord. The Washington City Paper covered its return two decades later on the Blue Period anthology.

years.h: Chad Clark takes the bad reviews hard
years.p: Chad Clark told Rolling Stone a Pitchfork review of the time felt negative, and for years he associated Beauty Pill's Dischord records with the feeling of failing.
years.xp: Looking back, Clark reframed it as a mismatch, not a verdict. He quoted a line from [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]: the last people to understand your new band are often the people who liked your old one.

years.h: Rachel Burke leaves; Jean Cook and Devin Ocampo join
years.p: Rachel Burke moves to Seattle and [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]] takes over vocals and strings. Drummer Ryan Nelson leaves to form [[Soccer Team|16cf8c3c-93a7-40a4-be20-460491346d49]] and [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]] replaces him.

eras.title: A virus in the heart
eras.text: Just as the new line-up settled, Clark nearly died. He kept the diagnosis private, survived emergency surgery, and spent two years recovering out of sight, making music the whole time and building a reading-and-music series on the side.

years.h: Chad Clark has emergency open-heart surgery
years.p: In fall 2007 Chad Clark contracted viral cardiomyopathy, a virus inflaming his heart, and told almost no one. It became public in February 2008 when he had emergency open-heart surgery.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the condition as rare. Rolling Stone later reported Clark left surgery with a battery-powered device keeping his heart going.

The surgery worked. Clark spent the next two years recovering privately, and writing, while Beauty Pill went quiet.

years.p: Chad Clark starts Story/Stereo, a DC performance series pairing writers and musicians. It goes on to win National Endowment for the Arts funding.

eras.title: Recording in public
eras.text: The comeback happened in a museum. Commissioned by Arlington's Artisphere, Beauty Pill turned the making of an album into an exhibit people could walk into, and the record that came out of it in 2015 put them on critics' year-end lists.

years.h: Beauty Pill Describes Things as They Are · Butterscotch
years.p: Beauty Pill recorded the album in public in 2011, as a residency at Artisphere in Arlington, Virginia. It came out in 2015 as a double LP, their first album away from Dischord.
years.xp:
The residency, called Immersive Ideal, turned the making of the album into an exhibit people could walk into; Wikipedia's album page says they finished a song a day. The line-up was the one with Chad Clark since 2005: Jean Cook, Devin Ocampo, Abram Goodrich, Basla Andolsun and Drew Doucette.

It made NPR's 50 best albums of 2015 and Rolling Stone's best albums you didn't hear. Magnet named it album of the year, Robert Christgau ranked it seventh, and Time later called it one of the ten best albums of the decade. Pitchfork, whose earlier review had stung, gave it a 7.5.

eras.title: A borrowed heart
eras.text: Beauty Pill became an art-space band, touring museums with Arto Lindsay and finally releasing the play score it had made in 2010. Then the heart device that had kept Chad Clark alive was recalled, and he needed a transplant.

years.p: Beauty Pill tour mostly museums and art spaces with Arto Lindsay, one of Chad Clark's heroes.

years.h: Beauty Pill's 2010 play score comes out, ten years late
years.p: In 2010 Beauty Pill scored suicide.chat.room, a play directed by Marcus Kyd. The score came out in 2020 as Sorry You're Here, alongside a new EP, Please Advise.
years.xp: Paulina Guerrero choreographed the play. The A.V. Club called the score brilliant and vividly balletic; the Washington Post, smartly evocative.

q: I'm borrowing [this heart] from some beautiful soul.
years.h: Chad Clark gets a new heart
years.p: After the manufacturer recalled his heart device, Chad Clark was hospitalized in spring 2022 and waited weeks for a donor heart that would fit a six-foot-four man. Rolling Stone reported he got a transplant that summer.
years.xp: Clark told Rolling Stone that everything he does for the rest of his life will be a risk.

years.h: Record Store Day reissue of Beauty Pill Describes Things as They Are
years.p: Beauty Pill's 2015 Artisphere album gets a Record Store Day reissue.
A double-album anthology of Beauty Pill's Dischord years: The Unsustainable Lifestyle, You Are Right to Be Afraid, outtakes and demos. Chad Clark had resisted revisiting the era for years.
